GLASS.TIMEOUT_DOC:
Timeout in seconds until Glassmeter screensaver starts.

Please set follow options in Touch Display plugin:
- The standard screensaver timeout in TouchScreen plugin should be set higher as than for Glass
-
- 'No Screensaver while playing' to 'ON'
GLASS.POSITION_TYPE_DOC: Where the theme goes on the screen, fitted or not: centred, or its top left at a position of your own.
GLASS.POSITION_FIT_DOC: Scale the theme to the screen, keeping its shape; the position below then places the scaled theme.
GLASS.ANIMATION_DOC: Animation on start and on stop of Glassmeter screensaver
GLASS.DISPLAY_DESC: Screensaver activation timeout, on-screen position, mouse pointer and which display output to use.
GLASS.PLAYBACK_DESC: Control display persistence during pause and track changes, and how animations react to playback progress (single track vs full queue)
GLASS.PERSIST_DURATION_DOC:
How long to keep Glass running when playback pauses or stops.

This prevents flicker during track changes and allows brief pauses without restarting the display.

Default: 30 seconds

Set to 'Disabled' for immediate stop (original behavior).
GLASS.PERSIST_DISPLAY_DOC:
What to show in the time display area when playback is paused.

Freeze: Keep last track time frozen (default)
Countdown: Show time until display turns off
GLASS.QUEUE_MODE_DOC:
How cassette reels and turntable tonearm react to playback progress.

Single Track: Animations based on current track duration (default)
Full Queue: Animations based on entire queue duration

Queue mode makes reels/tonearm move across the entire playlist. Falls back to track mode for webstreams or if queue is empty.
GLASS.VUMETER_DESC: Active meter selection plus signal response (smoothing, gain). Available meters depend on the selected theme.
GLASS.METER_DOC: Select one VU-Meter of active meter folder
GLASS.LIST_EMPTY: No VU-Meters in list. Revert back to random mode!
GLASS.RANDOMMODE_DOC: Switch of meters randomly on a defined timer interval or on change of music title
GLASS.RANDOMSELECTION_DOC:
Comma separated list of meter names for using, if 'List' selected.
Available meter list for copy and paste:
GLASS.RANDOMINTERVAL_DOC: Time interval until the next meter is displayed
GLASS.NEEDLE_CACHE_DOC:
All pictures of selected resolution are cached for a faster switch between styles in random mode.
The cache mode is only available for systems with at least 4GB installed memory
GLASS.CACHESIZE_DOC: Number of cached meters per selected resolution. Please be careful about increasing the value. An increased value requires more memory because more resources are cached. If there is not enough memory, the system may freeze.
GLASS.ACTIVE_FOLDER_DOC: Selection of the actively used folder for VU-Meter depend on screen resolution
GLASS.THEME_TAG_RULES_DOC: At the start of playback, the last [tag] in the album name or folder name selects a theme folder. Example: Vinyl=1920x1080_name_Vinyl, Tape=1920x1080_name_Tape. Text after the brackets is ignored, so [Vinyl] 2016 matches Vinyl. A word without brackets does not match. An empty list keeps the active meter folder.
GLASS.THEME_GALLERY_DESC: Preview and select installed meter themes. Selection applies immediately; use Active meter folder above to confirm or change again.
GLASS.THEMES_ARTWORK_DESC: Browse and select meter themes, remove installed themes, and configure the artist fanart slideshow. Saving applies the fanart settings; a theme is only removed when you explicitly pick one below.
GLASS.FANART_ENABLE_DOC: Show artist fanart in themes that declare a fanart area (fanart.pos / fanart.dim in meters.txt). Images come from your personal artist art folder, a 'fanart' subfolder next to the track, fanart.tv, then Volumio's artist art. This is a master switch: fanart only appears when this is on AND the active theme has a fanart area.
GLASS.FANART_KEY_MODE_DOC: Which fanart.tv API key to use. Personal key (recommended) uses your own key below. Project key uses the plugin's built-in key and is intended for testing / development only, not general use.
GLASS.FANART_KEY_DOC: Your own fanart.tv API key, used as the api_key when key mode is Personal. Required in Personal mode; if left blank, fanart.tv is skipped and the slideshow falls back to local art and Volumio's artist art. Register a project at fanart.tv to get a key (Account > API).
GLASS.FANART_INTERVAL_DOC: Automatically advance to the next fanart image every N seconds, counted from the last change; a new track changes the image as well. 0 means change only when the track changes. Range: 0 to 3600.
GLASS.FANART_ORDER_DOC: How the slideshow picks the next image. Sequential follows filename order (01, 02...). Random picks a different image each time. The current image is kept when random meter mode switches skins (same artist).
GLASS.FANART_TRANSITION_DOC: How the slideshow changes between images. None: instant cut. Fade in/out: the old image fades out, then the new one fades in. Merge: the two images cross-fade. Transitions apply to background-area fanart only; this is separate from the screensaver's start/stop transition.
GLASS.FANART_TRANSITION_MS_DOC: Length of the fanart transition in milliseconds. Range: 50 to 3000. Default 600.
GLASS.FANART_UNLIMITED_DOC: Default is a safe cap of 30 images per artist. When On, that cap is removed and every available image for the artist may be cached and shown. This can crash Glass Screensaver or Volumio (high RAM/CPU, especially on Raspberry Pi). Applies on the host and therefore to remote clients that use host fanart. Turn On only if you accept that risk. Apply shows a confirmation warning.
GLASS.FANART_UNLIMITED_CONFIRM_MSG:
Warning: this can crash Glass Screensaver or Volumio.

Removing the 30-image-per-artist limit lets the plugin cache and display every fanart file for an artist. Large sets use a lot of RAM and CPU (especially on Raspberry Pi) and can cause the screensaver or the whole device to freeze or crash.

This setting is stored on the Volumio host and also affects Glass Remote clients that load fanart from the host.

Confirm only if you understand and accept that risk. Cancel leaves the safe 30-image limit.
GLASS.FANART_UNLIMITED_CONFIRM_BTN: I accept the risk, enable unlimited
GLASS.FANART_UNLIMITED_ENABLED: Unlimited fanart images enabled. Fanart cache cleared; screensaver will reload. Use at your own risk.
GLASS.CLEAR_FANART_CACHE_DOC: Remove cached fanart copies from the device (fanart-cache). Use this after replacing images in your artist fanart folder if the slideshow still shows old photos. Local folder changes are normally picked up automatically on the next track; this forces an immediate refresh. MusicBrainz lookup data (mbid.json) is kept.
GLASS.CLEAR_FANART_CACHE_CONFIRM_MSG: This deletes cached fanart images on the device and restarts the screensaver so new artwork can load. Your source folders on the NAS or in /data/albumart/personal/artist/ are not touched.
GLASS.CLEAR_FANART_CACHE_DONE: Fanart cache cleared. The screensaver will reload with fresh artwork.
GLASS.BROWSE_THEMES_DOC: Open a gallery of preview images for installed themes. Uses preview.png (or preview.jpg / art.*) when present, otherwise meter.preview, screen.bgr, or bgr.filename from meters.txt.
GLASS.THEME_GALLERY_NONE: No theme preview images found. Add preview.png to theme folders, or set meter.preview, screen.bgr, or bgr.filename in meters.txt (see Skin Creation Guide).
GLASS.THEME_GALLERY_SELECT_HINT: Click a theme name under its preview to apply. The gallery closes automatically.
GLASS.THEME_GALLERY_INVALID: The selected theme folder is not valid.
GLASS.THEME_REMOVE_DOC: Select an installed theme to delete. It is removed from both the meter and spectrum templates. Deleted built-in themes return after a plugin update or reinstall.
GLASS.THEME_REMOVE_CONFIRM_MSG: This permanently deletes the theme folder from the meter and spectrum templates:
GLASS.THEME_REMOVE_INVALID: The selected theme cannot be removed.
GLASS.THEME_REMOVE_LAST: Cannot remove the last remaining theme.
GLASS.THEME_REMOVE_ACTIVE_RESET: Removed the active theme; switched to:
GLASS.METER_SENSITIVITY_DOC:
Adjust meter deflection without changing playback volume or the audio signal.

Default: 0 dB (no change)

Positive values boost quiet / ReplayGain-normalised material so needles move more. A library peaking near -9 dBFS reaches full scale around +9 dB.

Negative values reduce deflection when meters are overpowered (pinned at full scale). Useful to bring hot masters or high pipe levels back into a usable range.

Range: -12 to +12 dB. Levels above full scale are clamped, so the needle rests at maximum on the loudest passages when still too hot.
GLASS.MOUSE_DOC: For a touchscreen enable the mouse support, to have the possibility to stop the screensaver per touch. For a standard HDMI display without touch disable this option
GLASS.INTERACTIVE_DOC: A theme's play, mute, shuffle and repeat indicators, its volume and progress bars and its buttons act when tapped. As the theme says: the themes made for it. On: every theme that draws them. Off: a pure screensaver. A tap outside a control still does what the touch settings say.
GLASS.DISPLAY_OUTPUT_DOC: The X display the window opens on. 0 is the player's own screen.
GLASS.FORMAT_TYPE_MODE_DOC:
How to show the track format or streaming service in the type area.

Icon: Show the format icon (default; same as before)
Text: Show a text label (FLAC, Tidal, ...)
Both: Icon on the left and text on the right

A skin can override this with playinfo.type.mode in meters.txt.
GLASS.DO_NOT_DELETE_THEMES_DOC: When enabled: on uninstall the theme data folder is not removed; on install or update existing themes are not overwritten. Applies to all your custom themes (meters, spectrum, cassette, turntable, etc.).
GLASS.USE_SYSTEM_FONTS_DOC: Use Volumio system fonts (Lato) instead of built-in GlassFont. GlassFont includes universal language support (CJK, Arabic, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Thai, etc). Enable this only if you prefer the original fonts or have configured custom fonts in config.txt.
GLASS.SMB_SHARE_DESC: Share your template folders over the Volumio network share so you can edit and sync skins from another computer.
GLASS.SMB_SHARE_ACCESS: Allow template updates via network share
GLASS.SMB_SHARE_ACCESS_DOC:
Open file permissions on template folders so they can be updated via the Volumio network share (SMB/CIFS).

When enabled, templates and spectrum templates in Internal Storage can be synced from other devices using file managers like Beyond Compare, WinSCP, or any SMB client.

Permissions are normalized on every plugin start and settings save to catch newly uploaded files.
GLASS.INFO_MIN: The value has been adjusted to the lowest possible because the value entered is too small.
GLASS.INFO_MAX: The value has been adjusted to the highest possible because the value entered is too big.
GLASS.NAN: : The previous value was retained because the value entered is not a number.
GLASS.NO_PEPPYCONFIG: The configuration file is missing. Reinstall Glass.
GLASS.UNINSTALL_MSG: Please restart the system, when unistallation is complete
GLASS.NOMETERSWARNING_TITLE: You have selected an empty meters folder!
GLASS.NOMETERSWARNING: Please copy a valid meter template to resolution folder in: /data/INTERNAL/peppy_screensaver/templates
GLASS.NOTINLIST:
List cannot be saved.
Follow entries are not as meter section available:
GLASS.PERFORMANCE_DESC: How many frames a second the display draws. Turning records and reels look smoother at higher rates; needle meters need no more than 30.
GLASS.FRAME_RATE_DOC:
Display refresh rate in frames per second (FPS).

Default: 30

Lower values reduce CPU usage but may appear less smooth.
Recommended: 20-30 for Pi 4, 15-20 for Pi 3
GLASS.UPDATE_INTERVAL_DOC:
Spectrum and needle update frequency.

Default: 2 (updates every 2nd frame)

Higher values reduce CPU usage but decrease visual responsiveness.
At 30 FPS with interval 2: 15 updates/sec
At 20 FPS with interval 3: 6.7 updates/sec
GLASS.METER_DELAY_DOC:
Delay between render frames in milliseconds.

Default: 10

This setting balances CPU usage and meter responsiveness.

Higher values (10-20): Lower CPU usage, meters may feel slightly sluggish
Lower values (0-5): Higher CPU usage, more responsive meters

Warning: Values below 10 can significantly increase CPU usage (up to 95%).
Recommended: 10ms for most systems.
GLASS.DEBUG_LEVEL_DOC:
Controls logging to /tmp/peppy_debug.log

Off: No logging
Basic: Startup, errors, key state changes
Verbose: Configuration details (includes Basic)
Trace: Component-specific logging (use switches below)
GLASS.ANIMATION_DESC: Start/stop animation and fade transitions between meters and playback states
GLASS.TRANSITION_TYPE_DOC:
Visual transition when meter starts or stops.

None: Instant switch, no transition
Fade: Smooth fade in/out effect
GLASS.TRANSITION_DURATION_DOC:
Duration of fade transition in seconds.

Default: 0.5

Range: 0.1 to 5.0 seconds
GLASS.TRANSITION_COLOR_DOC:
Background color for fade transition.

Black: Fade from/to black (default)
White: Fade from/to white
GLASS.TRANSITION_OPACITY_DOC:
Opacity of the fade overlay.

100%: Solid color fade (default)
50%: Semi-transparent fade
0%: No fade effect

Range: 0 to 100%
GLASS.ROTATION_DESC: Album art and cassette spool rotation speed and quality
GLASS.ROTATION_QUALITY_DOC:
Controls smoothness vs CPU usage for rotating elements.

Low: 4 FPS, choppy, lowest CPU
Medium: 8 FPS, balanced (default)
High: 15 FPS, smooth, higher CPU
Custom: Set your own FPS
GLASS.ROTATION_FPS_DOC:
Custom rotation update rate.

Default: 8

Range: 4-30 FPS. Higher values use more CPU.
GLASS.ROTATION_SPEED_DOC:
Speed multiplier for spinning album art (vinyl skins).

1.0: Normal speed (default)
0.5: Half speed
2.0: Double speed

Range: 0.1 to 5.0
GLASS.SPOOL_LEFT_SPEED_DOC:
Speed multiplier for left cassette spool.

1.0: Normal speed (default)

Adjust separately from right spool for realistic effect.
GLASS.SPOOL_RIGHT_SPEED_DOC:
Speed multiplier for right cassette spool.

1.0: Normal speed (default)

Adjust separately from left spool for realistic effect.
GLASS.SPOOL_ADAPTIVE_DOC:
When enabled, cassette spool speeds change dynamically based on playback progress.

Left spool slows down as tape depletes, right spool speeds up as tape accumulates.

Uses queue progress when Queue Mode is set to Full Queue, otherwise uses single track progress.

Can be overridden per-meter in meters.txt with spool.adaptive = true/false
GLASS.REEL_DIRECTION_DOC:
Rotation direction for cassette spools.

Counter-clockwise: Standard direction (default)
Clockwise: Reverse direction
GLASS.SCROLLING_DESC: Text scrolling speed for artist, title, and album display
GLASS.SCROLLING_MODE_DOC:
How to determine text scrolling speed.

Use skin value: Use speed defined in skin (or 40 if not set)
System default: Always use 40 pixels/sec
Custom: Set individual speeds for each field
GLASS.SCROLLING_SPEED_ARTIST_DOC:
Scrolling speed for artist text in pixels per second.

Default: 40

Lower values = slower scrolling. Range: 5-200
GLASS.SCROLLING_SPEED_TITLE_DOC:
Scrolling speed for title text in pixels per second.

Default: 40

Lower values = slower scrolling. Range: 5-200
GLASS.SCROLLING_SPEED_ALBUM_DOC:
Scrolling speed for album text in pixels per second.

Default: 40

Lower values = slower scrolling. Range: 5-200
GLASS.TRACE_METERS_DOC: Log audio levels, needle position calculations, and render decisions
GLASS.TRACE_SPECTRUM_DOC: Log spectrum init, update calls, and thread lifecycle
GLASS.TRACE_VINYL_DOC: Log vinyl rotation state, angle, FPS gating, and skip reasons
GLASS.TRACE_REEL_LEFT_DOC: Log left cassette reel state, angle, and render decisions
GLASS.TRACE_REEL_RIGHT_DOC: Log right cassette reel state, angle, and render decisions
GLASS.TRACE_TONEARM_DOC: Log tonearm state machine, progress input, angle calculations, and transitions
GLASS.TRACE_ALBUMART_DOC: Log album art URL changes, rotation, cache hits/misses
GLASS.TRACE_SCROLLING_DOC: Log artist/title/album scroll position and wrap events
GLASS.TRACE_VOLUME_DOC: Log volume value changes and slider/knob position calculations
GLASS.TRACE_REPEAT_DOC: Log repeat state changes (off, all, single)
GLASS.TRACE_PROGRESS_DOC: Log progress percentage and seek input
GLASS.TRACE_METADATA_DOC: Log every pushState event from Volumio with all values
GLASS.TRACE_SEEK_DOC: Log raw vs interpolated seek, elapsed time calculations
GLASS.TRACE_TIME_DOC: Log time remaining calculations and display updates
GLASS.TRACE_INIT_DOC: Log meter initialization, backing captures, renderer creation
GLASS.TRACE_FADE_DOC: Log fade in/out timing, lock states, skip reasons
GLASS.TRACE_FRAME_DOC: Log render loop timing, status changes, FPS gating
GLASS.TRACE_REMOTE_DOC: Log remote display server activity including client connections, disconnections, heartbeats, and unknown traffic.
GLASS.TRACE_REMOTE_PACKETS_DOC: Log every packet sent and received by the remote server. Warning: High volume output - use only for debugging data flow issues.
GLASS.PROFILING_DESC: CPU performance analysis tools for identifying bottlenecks
GLASS.PROFILING_TIMING_DOC:
Log time breakdown for each render frame to /tmp/peppy_debug.log

Shows: total frame time, meter, rotation, blit, scroll, and other components.

Low overhead - safe for continuous use during testing.
GLASS.PROFILING_INTERVAL_DOC:
Log timing every N frames.

1: Every frame (verbose)
30: Once per second at 30fps (default)
300: Every 10 seconds

Lower values = more log output
GLASS.PROFILING_CPROFILE_DOC:
Full Python function-level profiling.

WARNING: Significant CPU overhead (10-30%). Only use for short diagnostic sessions.

Creates /tmp/peppy_profile.prof and /tmp/peppy_profile_summary.txt on exit.
GLASS.PROFILING_DURATION_DOC:
Auto-stop cProfile after this many seconds.

0: Run until meter stops (not recommended)
60: One minute (default)
300: Five minutes

Prevents runaway profile file growth.
GLASS.REMOTE_DESC: Stream audio levels to remote displays over the network
GLASS.REMOTE_SERVER_ENABLED_DOC:
Enable streaming of audio levels to remote displays.

When enabled, this device will broadcast audio level data over the network for remote Glass displays to receive.
GLASS.REMOTE_SERVER_MODE_DOC:
How to operate when remote server is enabled.

Server Only: Stream levels to remote displays, no local display (headless)
Server + Local: Both stream to remote displays AND show local display

Remote displays connect using run_peppy_remote.py on another Pi.
GLASS.REMOTE_DISCOVERY_PORT_DOC:
UDP port for auto-discovery broadcasts.

Default: 5579

Remote clients listen on this port to find the server automatically.
GLASS.REMOTE_SERVER_PORT_DOC:
UDP port for streaming audio level data to remote displays.

Default: 5580

Change if this port conflicts with other services.
GLASS.REMOTE_SPECTRUM_PORT_DOC:
UDP port for streaming spectrum analyzer data to remote displays.

Default: 5581

Change if this port conflicts with other services.
GLASS.REMOTE_SPECTRUM_ALWAYS_DOC:
When the host meter has no spectrum, still read the spectrum FIFO and send bins to remotes (Server + Local mode).

Off (default): Spectrum UDP follows the host meter only. If the host skin has no spectrum, remotes get no bins, best when host and remote meters stay in sync.
On: Remotes can show a live spectrum even when the host meter has none (e.g. random/list or different local templates). Uses exclusive FIFO handoff so the host display does not flicker.

Has no effect in Server Only (headless) mode, which always streams spectrum.
GLASS.CONFIG_SYNC_INTERVAL_DOC:
How often to check for config changes and notify remote clients.

Default: 1 second

Lower values mean remote clients detect changes faster. Range: 1-60 seconds.
GLASS.BACKUP_DESC: Continuity Engine - save and restore your plugin settings across reinstalls
GLASS.BACKUP_SECTION_RESTORE_DESC: Replace current plugin settings with a saved snapshot. The meter will restart to apply the restored settings.
GLASS.BACKUP_SECTION_DELETE_DESC: Permanently remove a saved snapshot from Internal Storage.
GLASS.BACKUP_INFO: Create a named backup of all plugin settings (config.json, meter.txt, spectrum.txt). Backups are stored in Internal Storage and survive plugin uninstall/reinstall, so you can pick up where you left off after an update or a fresh install. Pick a backup from the list below to restore or delete it.
GLASS.BACKUP_NAME_DOC: A short descriptive name for the new backup (for example: 'studio setup', 'christmas', 'gelo5 experiment'). Letters, digits, spaces, dots, hyphens and underscores only. Max 64 characters.
GLASS.BACKUP_CREATE_DOC: Save current plugin settings as a new backup under the name typed above.
GLASS.BACKUP_SELECTED_DOC: Choose an existing backup to restore or delete. Newest first.
GLASS.BACKUP_RESTORE_DOC: Replace current plugin settings with the selected backup. The meter will restart to apply the restored settings.
GLASS.BACKUP_DELETE_DOC: Permanently remove the selected backup from Internal Storage.
GLASS.BACKUP_NAME_REQUIRED: Please enter a name for the backup first.
GLASS.BACKUP_NAME_INVALID: Invalid backup name. Use letters, digits, spaces, dots, hyphens and underscores only (max 64 characters).
GLASS.BACKUP_NAME_EXISTS: A backup with this name already exists. Delete the existing one first or pick a different name.
GLASS.BACKUP_DISK_FULL: Not enough free space in Internal Storage to create a new backup.
GLASS.BACKUP_COUNT_WARN: You have 20 or more backups. Consider deleting old ones to keep the list manageable.
GLASS.BACKUP_SOURCE_MISSING: A required source file is missing and cannot be backed up
GLASS.BACKUP_CREATE_FAILED: Failed to create backup. Check the log for details.
GLASS.BACKUP_NOT_FOUND: The selected backup could not be found.
GLASS.BACKUP_MANIFEST_INVALID: Backup manifest is missing or invalid. This backup cannot be restored.
GLASS.BACKUP_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED: This backup was created by a newer version of the plugin and cannot be restored. Please update the plugin first.
GLASS.BACKUP_FILES_MISSING: Backup files are missing. This backup cannot be restored.
GLASS.BACKUP_CONFIG_CORRUPT: Backup config.json is corrupted and cannot be restored.
GLASS.BACKUP_PEPPYCONF_CORRUPT: The backup's meter.txt is corrupted and cannot be restored.
GLASS.BACKUP_SPECTRUMCONF_CORRUPT: The backup's spectrum.txt is corrupted and cannot be restored.
GLASS.BACKUP_RESTORED: Backup restored. Meter will reload on next playback.
GLASS.BACKUP_RESTORE_FAILED: Failed to restore backup. Check the log for details.
GLASS.BACKUP_DELETE_FAILED: Failed to delete backup. Check the log for details.
GLASS.LEGACY_ENABLED_MSG: Glass replaces PeppyMeter Screensaver and cannot run while that plugin is enabled, so Glass stays disabled. Use the button here, or disable PeppyMeter Screensaver in Plugins and then enable Glass.
GLASS.LEGACY_DISABLE_BTN: Disable PeppyMeter Screensaver and start Glass
GLASS.LEGACY_DISABLED: PeppyMeter Screensaver disabled. Glass is starting.
GLASS.LEGACY_DISABLE_FAILED: PeppyMeter Screensaver could not be disabled. Disable it in Plugins, then enable Glass.
GLASS.IMPORTED_SETTINGS: Settings taken over from PeppyMeter Screensaver.
GLASS.RESTART_TITLE: Restart to finish setting up Glass
GLASS.RESTART_MSG: The meters read the audio through an ALSA chain that Volumio builds from the plugins it knew at start. Glass joins that chain after a restart; until then the display shows no levels.
GLASS.MANAGER_DESC: Themes, the catalog, artwork, backups and the status of the display are managed in the Glass Manager, a page the plugin serves on its own port.
GLASS.MANAGER_OPEN_DOC: Opens the manager in this window, inside Volumio's own page.
GLASS.MANAGER_OPEN_TAB: Open the manager in a new tab
GLASS.MANAGER_OPEN_TAB_DOC: Opens the manager in a browser tab of its own. Its address:
GLASS.THEMES_DESC: The theme on show, the edition tag rules, and whether themes survive an uninstall. Installing, previewing and removing themes is done in the Glass Manager.
GLASS.CLEAR_FANART_CACHE_FAILED: The fanart cache could not be cleared.
GLASS.MANAGER_METER_NAMES: Pick at least one meter, or exactly one for a single meter.
GLASS.MANAGER_METER_UNKNOWN: The theme has no meter named:
GLASS.MANAGER_DISPLAY_DOC: Where the theme goes on the screen: fitted to it, scaled with its shape kept, or pixel for pixel; centred, or with its top left at a position of your own. The display starts again with the change.
GLASS.MANAGER_DISPLAY_FIT: Fit the theme to the screen
GLASS.MANAGER_LEGACY_DOC: The old plugin's folder still holds {n} themes, {mb} MB. Glass copied them once at its first install and reads its own folder; they only take space now. Wiping removes the old plugin's templates and templates_spectrum folders and nothing else.
GLASS.MANAGER_LEGACY_INSTALLED: PeppyMeter Screensaver is still installed: its display would have no themes left.
GLASS.MANAGER_LEGACY_CONFIRM_MSG: This removes them for good. Glass's own themes stay as they are.
GLASS.MANAGER_LEGACY_DONE: The old plugin's themes are gone.
GLASS.MANAGER_TAILOR_DOC: A copy of this theme cut to another screen size and installed beside it: every position, size, length and font size scaled, every picture resampled, the theme's shape kept and the copy centred on the new screen. The size offered is the theme on show, which is what your screen shows; change it for another screen.
GLASS.MANAGER_TAILOR_STRETCH: Stretch to the screen's shape instead of keeping the theme's
GLASS.MANAGER_PACKAGE_STARTED: Packaging, the meters are shown one by one for the preview:
GLASS.MANAGER_JOB_PACKAGING: packaging, a preview of every meter
GLASS.MANAGER_PACKAGE_PROGRESS: {done} of {total} meters shown, about {s} s to go
GLASS.MANAGER_FACE_ANYMOTE_HELP: Anymote, any remote, a remote from anywhere, is the same face on a page of its own, /anymote on this port, for any browser: it fills the window, one tap takes the screen, and a phone or a tablet keeps it on the home screen as a full-screen app. Taps and drags on the theme's controls act on the player when the controls are on.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_PICK: What is wrong? Pick what comes closest; the Manager checks what it can see for itself.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_S_NOT_MOVING: The meters show but do not move
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_S_RESTARTS: The display dies at once or keeps restarting
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_S_TOUCH: Touch or the controls do not act as they should
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_S_SCREEN: The picture is turned, cropped or in the wrong place
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_S_ARTWORK: Album art, fanart or folder pictures are missing
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_S_REMOTES: A remote display, the Face or Anymote does not show or move
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_S_SLOW: It is slow, or the player is busy
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_FOUND: The checks found a likely cause. If that is not it, make a report.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_NOTHING: The checks found no cause. Make a report: it carries these findings, the status sheet and the player's system log.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_V_FOUND: the checks found a likely cause
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_REPORT_INTRO: A report holds what the checks found, the status sheet, your own words and a link to the player's system log. To catch the problem in that log, Glass logs in full while you reproduce it, and the display starts again; the log level goes back by itself afterwards. Then the player's system log, its journal, configuration and network details with passwords left out, is sent to Volumio's log server, the way the player's own dev page sends it.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_CAPTURING: Glass is logging in full since {from}, until {until} at the latest. Do now what goes wrong. When it has happened, say what you did and what you saw, and press the button.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_SAID: What you did, and what you saw
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_SAID_NEEDED: Say in a line what you did and what you saw.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_HAPPENED: It has happened: make the report
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_SENDING: Sending the player's system log to Volumio's log server…
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_REPORT_READY: The report is ready. Open a GitHub issue with it for a defect, with the evidence it holds; copy it into a post on the community forum for a question or anything else.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_REPORT_NO_LINK: The report is ready, without a link: the system log could not be sent ({said}). Where a download is offered, attach that file to your issue or post.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_R_SAID: What I did and what I saw
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_R_WINDOW: Reproduced between {from} and {to} by the player's clock, as in the log, with Glass logging in full.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_ISSUE_PASTE: The full report is on your clipboard: paste it here.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_RELEASE_NEWER: Glass {latest} is out and this player runs {current}. Later versions fix known problems: upgrade on the System tab first.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_LEGACY_ON: PeppyMeter Screensaver is enabled beside Glass. Only one of the two may run: disable it under Plugins, Installed Plugins.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_NO_BINARY: The display's binary for this player ({arch}) is missing from the plugin. Install the zip from the releases page again.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_DISK_FULL: The player's storage is nearly full: {mb} MB free. Themes, previews and upgrades need room.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_JOURNAL_PROBLEMS:
Glass's last warnings in the journal:
{lines}
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_HEADLESS: The display output is set to "No screen of its own": Glass opens no window on purpose. Choose the player's screen in the Display section of the settings page.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_NOT_PLAYING: The player is not playing ({status}). The meters appear, and move, only while it plays; they open {timeout} s after playback begins.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_KIOSK_FAILED: The kiosk service has failed, so there is no X server to draw on. Turn the Touch Display plugin off and on again, or restart the player.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_NO_PANEL: No panel is connected and no X server runs: the display has nothing to draw on. Check the screen's cable and power.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_KIOSK_ON_ITS_WAY: The kiosk is on its way (service: {kiosk}) and no X server is up yet: the display waits for it and opens no window meanwhile.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_DISPLAY_UP: The display is on the screen.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_DISPLAY_NOT_UP: The player plays and the display is not on the screen. It opens {timeout} s after playback begins. If it stays away, the log on the System tab says why.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_LOG_WRONG_BINARY: The launcher says the display's binary is missing or is for another CPU ({arch}). Install the zip from the releases page for this player.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_LOG_NO_WINDOW: The display could not open its window ({count} times since the player started): no X server at the display number chosen, or the kiosk was not running.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_LOG_DIED: The display died {count} times since the player started. The last: {last}. The lines before it in the log, on the System tab, say what went wrong.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_LOG_NO_DEATHS: No display death in Glass's {lines} lines since the player started.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_TAP_IN: The audio tap heads the sound path.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_TAP_OUT: The audio tap is not in the sound path, so nothing is measured. Restart the player once: the start rebuilds the path.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_NOT_MEASURED: What plays ({service}) is not measured: it reaches the sound card below the audio tap, heard but not seen. For Spotify Connect, AirPlay or Soloist, restart that plugin; for files and radio, restart the player once.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_INTERACTIVE_OFF: Interactive controls are off: no tap on a theme's controls acts. Set them on the System tab.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_INTERACTIVE_THEME: Interactive controls act as the theme says: only a meter with interactive = True, or with buttons, takes taps. "On" on the System tab acts for every theme that draws indicators.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_INTERACTIVE_ON: Interactive controls are on for every theme.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_POINTING: The player has something to point with: {names}.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_NO_POINTING: The player reports no touch panel and no mouse, so nothing can tap. Check the panel's touch cable and whether the system sees the panel.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_TOUCH_UNDER_KIOSK: The kiosk's X server maps touch on this screen, and Glass takes it from there; Glass's own touch mapping applies only where it draws on the screen itself. Touches that land wrong here are set in the Touch Display plugin.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_CALIBRATION_FAILED: The last touch calibration failed, and the map before it is in use. Calibrate again on the Screen tab, touching the centre of each target.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_TOUCH_MAP_AUTO: Touch is taken as the panel reports it. If touches land in the wrong place, try swap or mirror on the Screen tab, then calibrate.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_TOUCH_MAP_SET: Touch is mapped by your setting ({mapping}). If touches land in the wrong place, calibrate on the Screen tab or go back to "As the panel reports".
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_CHANNEL_UP: The display is connected to the player: taps reach it.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_CHANNEL_DOWN: The display is up and not connected to the plugin's channel, so a tap cannot reach the player. The log on the System tab says why.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_SCREEN_GLASS: The screen is Glass's own: no kiosk uses it, and the Screen tab's controls apply.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_SCREEN_KIOSK: The kiosk holds this screen and turns the picture itself; Glass draws over it as a screensaver. The Screen tab's rotation, pointer and touch controls apply only on a player with no kiosk, and are hidden here on purpose. The rotation is set in the Touch Display plugin.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_ROTATION_AS_SUGGESTED: The rotation ({rotation}) is what the panel suggests.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_ROTATION_PORTRAIT: The panel ({panel}) is portrait by nature and the rotation is 0, so the picture stands on its side or is cropped. Set the rotation to {suggested} on the Screen tab; touch turns with it.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_ROTATION_DIFFERS: The rotation is {rotation}; the panel ({panel}) suggests {suggested}.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_THEME_SIZE: The theme is drawn for {theme} and the screen is {screen}. Fit to screen on the Appearance tab scales it; a theme of the screen's own size costs less.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_FANART_OFF: Artist fanart is off. Turn it on on the Appearance tab; the theme needs a place for it too (fanart.pos).
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_FANART_COSTS: Artist fanart is on: a slideshow with fades costs processor time and memory. Try with it off on the Appearance tab.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_ARTWORK_PLACES: A picture shows only where the theme has a place for it: albumart.pos for the album art, fanart.pos for fanart, folderlayer.N.files for pictures from the track's folder, named exactly as the files are. A stream has no folder.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_SERVING_OFF: Remote displays are not served: the switch on the Remotes tab is off. The Face and Anymote do not need it.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_SERVING_DOWN: Remote displays are switched on and not served: {problem}. The Remotes tab says which port is taken.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_SERVING: Remote displays are served: frames on port {frames}, the channel on {channel}.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_NO_REMOTES: No remote is connected. A remote on another network does not hear the player's beacon: add the player by name or address on the remote's own page.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_NOT_RECEIVING: {connected} remotes are connected and {receiving} receive frames: UDP to port {port} is blocked between the machines, or the remote started before the port was moved.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_FACE_NO_FRAMES: A Face page is open, the player plays and is measured, and no frames reach the page: the frames daemon is not running or not reachable. Restart the player's backend once.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_FACE_RESTS: A Face page is open and gets no frames because nothing measured is playing: it moves when the player does.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_GOVERNED: The display lowered its frame rate to {rate} from the {set} set: the theme costs more than the player has. A lower rate or a lighter profile on the System tab, or a smaller theme, costs less.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_RATE_ABOVE_BOARD: The frame rate is {rate}; {suits} suits this board ({board}). The profile on the System tab sets it.
GLASS.MANAGER_DIAG_RATE_SUITS: The frame rate ({rate}) suits this board ({board}).
GLASS.MANAGER_ST_TAP_IN: the tap heads the ALSA chain
GLASS.MANAGER_ST_TAP_OUT: the tap is not in the ALSA chain: restart the player
GLASS.MANAGER_FACE_HELP: The meters as the player shows them, drawn here by the same engine: the theme on show, the meter it shows, the levels as they play. Any browser on the network can watch, a phone or a tablet too. The theme is kept in this browser and fetched again only when it changes.
GLASS.MANAGER_FACE_NO_MODULE: this release has no browser module; upgrade Glass
GLASS.MANAGER_FACE_NO_FRAMES: no frames: the frames daemon is not running
GLASS.MANAGER_FACE_STOPPED: The player is stopped. The display has left the screen; the meters return when it plays.
GLASS.MANAGER_FACE_PAUSED: The player is paused. The display has left the screen; the meters return when it plays.
GLASS.MANAGER_FONTS_HELP: Each text style is set in a face of your choice: the built-in multi-script face (Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai, the Indic scripts, Chinese, Japanese and Korean), a font you uploaded, or one of the player's own. A character a face lacks is taken from the built-in regular face. The display starts again with a change.
GLASS.MANAGER_FONTS_MISSING: The built-in set is not on this player.
GLASS.MANAGER_FONTS_CUSTOM_DOC: A TrueType or OpenType file (.ttf, .otf), one face per file, kept on the player through updates. Remotes bring uploaded fonts from the player with the other fonts.
GLASS.MANAGER_FONTS_REMOVE_MSG: A style set in it goes back to the built-in face. This deletes the file from the player:
GLASS.MANAGER_FONTS_NOT_A_FONT: That file is not a TrueType or OpenType font.
GLASS.MANAGER_FONTS_BAD_CHOICE: That font is not on the player.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_HELP: Two themes by the clock: the day theme from one time, the night theme from another, put on show by the player itself, at the times and after a start. For a screen in a car, or a dark theme for the evening in a room. Remotes that follow the player follow the switch.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_NOW_DAY: Day now, the theme on show is
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_NOW_NIGHT: Night now, the theme on show is
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_OFF: Off: the theme on show stays as chosen on this tab.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_ERR_TIME: A time is HH:MM on the 24 hour clock.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_ERR_SAME: The day and the night start at the same time.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_ERR_THEME: Choose an installed theme for the day and one for the night.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_MODE_CLOCK: By the clock, at the two times
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_MODE_SUN: By the sun, at sunrise and sunset
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_OFFSET: Minutes after sunset and before sunrise
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_LOCATION_ZONE: The place of the player's time zone:
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_LOCATION_NONE: No place is known for the player's time zone.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_LOCATION_DOC: A latitude and longitude of your own, for the minute, or where the zone's place is far away; a car within its zone needs none. On a day without a sunrise or sunset, the two times apply.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_NO_SUN: no sunrise or sunset here today, the two times apply
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_ERR_LOCATION: A latitude is -90 to 90 and a longitude -180 to 180, both or neither.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_ERR_NO_LOCATION: No place is known for the player's time zone: enter a latitude and longitude.
GLASS.MANAGER_CD_ERR_OFFSET: The offset is at most 180 minutes either way.
GLASS.MANAGER_PREVIEWS: Meters, as the display draws them
GLASS.MANAGER_ROTATION_HELP: Which meters of this theme the display shows, and when it moves to the next one. The rotation belongs to the theme on show.
GLASS.MANAGER_REPLACE_MSG: The files in these folders are replaced by the ones from the catalog:
GLASS.MANAGER_CATALOG_ERROR: The catalog could not be fetched:
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_CHECKSUM: The download does not match the catalog checksum.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_SIZE: The download has the wrong size.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_UNITS: The zip does not hold the folders the catalog names.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_BAD_THEME: The zip is not a theme.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_NOT_ZIP: The file is not a zip.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_TOO_LARGE: The file is larger than allowed.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_RENDER: The display could not draw the previews.
GLASS.MANAGER_UNLIMITED_HELP: Without the cap of 30 images per artist, every available image is cached and shown. Large sets use a lot of memory and processor, especially on a Raspberry Pi.
GLASS.MANAGER_UNLIMITED_CONFIRM: Removing the 30-image cap lets the plugin cache and show every fanart file for an artist. Large sets use a lot of memory and processor, especially on a Raspberry Pi, and can freeze the display or the player. The setting is stored on the player and reaches Glass Remote clients that load fanart from it.
GLASS.MANAGER_CLEAR_CACHE_MSG: The cached fanart images on the player are deleted and the display reloads. The source folders are not touched.
GLASS.MANAGER_ST_NO_BINARY: no display binary for this machine
GLASS.MANAGER_UPD_CHECK_FAILED: The release could not be checked:
GLASS.MANAGER_UPD_CONFIRM_MSG: A settings backup is written and the installed plugin is kept for going back. The plugin is then replaced by the release and the player’s backend restarts: music keeps playing, the display and this page come back within a minute.
GLASS.MANAGER_UPD_ROLLBACK_MSG: The plugin is put back to the version kept from the last upgrade and the player’s backend restarts. Music keeps playing; the display and this page come back within a minute.
GLASS.MANAGER_UPD_WAITING: waiting for Glass to come back
GLASS.MANAGER_UPD_NOT_BACK: Glass has not come back yet. Reload this page in a minute.
GLASS.MANAGER_UPD_LAST_FAILED: The last upgrade did not take:
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_NO_RELEASE: No release with a plugin zip was found.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_NO_DIGEST: The release carries no checksum for its zip.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_APPLY: The player’s plugin manager could not replace the plugin.
GLASS.MANAGER_UPD_TEST_HELP: A test release is built and published, and still being tried on the project’s own players before it is offered to everyone. With this on, this player is offered Glass and glass-evo as soon as they are published. Going back to the kept version works as ever.
GLASS.MANAGER_ERR_BAD_BACKUP: The zip is not a Glass settings backup.
GLASS.MANAGER_PORT_DOC: The port the manager listens on, 5582 unless another service on this player uses it. A change applies at once: the manager moves to the new port and the buttons follow.
GLASS.MANAGER_HOST_DOC: How browsers reach this player. Empty uses the player's name with .local, which mDNS resolves on most networks. Enter the player's IP address or a host name when .local names do not resolve on yours.
GLASS.MANAGER_PORT_INVALID: The manager port must be a number from 1024 to 65535.
GLASS.MANAGER_PORT_IN_USE: That port is in use by something else on this player. The manager stays on port
GLASS.MANAGER_HOST_INVALID: The manager address must be a host name or an IP address, without http:// or a port.
GLASS.MANAGER_MOVED: The manager now listens on port
GLASS.MANAGER_ST_NOT_MEASURED: not measured: the source plays below the tap
GLASS.MANAGER_RM_HELP: A remote display is Glass on another machine, showing this player's meters with this player's theme or with one of its own choosing. It finds the player by its beacon or by name, takes the frames over the network, and is set up on a page of its own, linked below when it serves one. Run it with: glass --remote
GLASS.MANAGER_RM_OFF: Remote displays are off on this player.
GLASS.DISPLAY_OUTPUT_NONE: No screen of its own: remote displays only
GLASS.MANAGER_RM_ENABLE_DOC: When on, this player sends its frames to remote displays that subscribe, serves them the channel, and announces itself on the network. Off, nothing leaves the player. Ports are taken at once when applied; a port something else holds is reported here.
GLASS.MANAGER_RM_PORTS_INVALID: Ports must be numbers from 1024 to 65535.
GLASS.MANAGER_RM_PORTS_CLASH: The three ports and the manager's port must all differ.
GLASS.MANAGER_TOUCH_HELP: A theme's play, mute, shuffle and repeat indicators, its volume and progress bars and its buttons act when tapped, on the player's screen and on remotes. As the theme says: on for the meters that ask for it. On: every theme that draws them. Off: a pure screensaver. A tap outside a control still does what the touch settings say. The display starts again with the change.
GLASS.MANAGER_SCREEN_HELP: How the picture is turned and whether the pointer shows, on a screen Glass draws on itself. Glass draws on X while the kiosk runs one, on the screen itself (KMS/DRM) while no kiosk uses it, and steps aside the moment the kiosk comes back.
GLASS.MANAGER_SCREEN_DETAILS: The screen's details on the Status tab
GLASS.MANAGER_SCREEN_WOULD_DRAW: The display is not on the screen now; when it starts it draws on
GLASS.MANAGER_SCREEN_WOULD_DRAW_NOTHING: The display is not on the screen now, and would open no window: the kiosk is on its way, or no panel is connected.
GLASS.MANAGER_SCREEN_FREE: The screen is Glass's: no kiosk, no X server. The display stays on it, and the controls below apply.
GLASS.MANAGER_SCREEN_OWN_X: The screen is Glass's, through an X server brought up for it: no kiosk, no browser. The display stays on it, and the controls below apply.
GLASS.MANAGER_SCREEN_NOT_FREE: The kiosk is the player's interface on this screen. Glass runs as a screensaver over it and leaves it be; the screen's own controls apply only when no kiosk uses it.
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_KIOSK: The kiosk owns the screen: it is the player's interface, Glass a screensaver over it.
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_EVO: glass-evo owns the screen: it is the player's interface; the kiosk and what runs it are off, recorded below.
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_NO_BINARY: installed, but without a binary for this player
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_ERROR: The last change did not finish:
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_BACK: Give the screen back to the kiosk
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_CONFIRM_TAKE: glass-evo takes the screen. The kiosk and the plugins that run it are turned off, each through its own plugin manager, and recorded so that they come back the same way. Go on?
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_CONFIRM_BACK: The kiosk gets the screen back. What glass-evo turned off is turned on again, in reverse order, where it is still as it was left. Go on?
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_EVO_ABSENT: glass-evo is not installed for this player.
GLASS.MANAGER_FACE_SIZE_LARGE: Large, for a hand at arm's length
GLASS.MANAGER_FACE_SIZE_CAR: Car, for a glance while driving
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_LEAD: Glass's own interface for the player's screen, in the kiosk's place: playback controls, a clock and looks over the meters, with browse and the queue to follow. Getting it changes nothing on the screen: the choice is made on the Screen tab, and the kiosk comes back whenever the screen is given back. A preview: verified on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a DSI screen and on x86; on any screen the way back is here, from any browser.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_REMOVE_MSG: glass-evo and the version kept for going back are removed from the player. Face themes of your own and your adjustments stay.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_KIOSK: The kiosk owns the screen. It is handed to glass-evo on the Screen tab.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_OUTDATED: Older than this Glass works with: update it to
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_BEHIND: The latest release is older than this Glass works with, which is
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_INSTALL_MSG: The release is downloaded from GitHub, checked against its checksum and installed; the version in place is kept for going back. A face on the screen starts again as the new one.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_ROLLBACK_MSG: The version kept is put back, and the one in place is kept instead. A face on the screen starts again.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_ERR_OWNS_SCREEN: glass-evo owns the screen: give the screen back to the kiosk first, on the Screen tab.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_ERR_NEEDS_GLASS: This glass-evo needs a later Glass: upgrade Glass first.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_ERR_TOO_OLD: This glass-evo is older than this Glass works with.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_ERR_NO_BINARY: This glass-evo has no binary for this player.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_ERR_PAIR: Glass and glass-evo could not be brought to versions that work together.
GLASS.MANAGER_EVO_ERR_MANIFEST: The download is not a glass-evo component.
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_OWN_X: it brought up an X server of its own
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_NO_SCREEN: This player has no screen glass-evo can draw on by itself: its picture comes only through the kiosk. The kiosk stays the interface here.
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_BACK_FACE_FAILED: glass-evo could not start, so the screen went back to the kiosk.
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_BACK_COMPONENT_MISSING: The glass-evo component was gone, so the screen went back to the kiosk.
GLASS.MANAGER_OWNER_BACK_PLUGIN_STOPPED: Glass was turned off, so the screen went back to the kiosk.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_LEAD: Choose a look. You can adjust it underneath.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_PREVIEW_HELP: A likeness of the player's screen. The buttons show when the screen is touched. Click a part to adjust it.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_PLAIN: Back to the look as it comes
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_HIGHLIGHT_HINT: What is switched on, such as repeat.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_BLUR_HEAVY: Heavy for this player: turn it off if the screen stutters.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_MORE_PIECE: More: its own colour and background…
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_SAVE_NOTE: The player's screen changes when you save.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_RESET_ASK: The screen goes back to the look it came with, the one that follows the artwork, and every adjustment is removed.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_RESET_DONE: The screen is back to the look it came with.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOOK_PATTERN_HINT: A pattern says what shows and in which order: %H hours, %I hours of twelve, %M minutes, %S seconds, %p AM or PM, %A the day, %a the day short, %d the day of the month, %B the month, %b the month short, %m the month as a number, %Y the year. A minus drops a leading zero: %-d.
GLASS.MANAGER_TOUCHMAP_HELP: How a finger's place on the panel becomes a place on the picture. As the panel reports it is right for most panels. A panel whose touch frame is swapped or mirrored against the picture takes the overrides. A panel that reports something else is calibrated: the display shows five targets on the screen, you touch each once, and the map that undoes the panel is kept. The rotation of the screen is applied after this, so calibrate in the orientation you use.
GLASS.MANAGER_TOUCHMAP_CALIBRATE_HELP: The player's screen shows a target; touch its centre once, then the next, five in all. The display must be on the screen: start the music first if it is not.
GLASS.MANAGER_TOUCHMAP_STARTED: Targets on the screen: touch each once.
GLASS.MANAGER_TOUCHMAP_WAITING: Waiting for the touches on the screen…
GLASS.MANAGER_TOUCHMAP_FAIL_UNFIT: the touches did not fit one map; touch the centre of each target.
GLASS.MANAGER_TOUCHMAP_FAIL_NOCONFIG: the configuration could not be written.
GLASS.MANAGER_TOUCH_NOT_CALIBRATED: No calibration is kept yet: calibrate on the screen first.
GLASS.MANAGER_SHARE_HELP: Volumio shares its Internal Storage folder on the network, and the theme folders live in it. With this on, they are writable from any computer on the share, for editing a theme in place; off, they can be read over the share but not changed.
GLASS.MANAGER_SHARE_ON: Let computers on the network edit the themes
GLASS.MANAGER_SHARE_ON_DOC: Applies to every theme folder now and to the ones installed later. The share is \\<player>\Internal Storage; the themes are under glass\templates, with glass\templates_spectrum beside it.
GLASS.MANAGER_PERF_HELP: A profile sets the frame rate, the rotation quality and the transitions together. Auto picks one for this board; Custom keeps what the settings page says.
GLASS.MANAGER_PERF_APPLIED: Applied. The display starts again with it.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOG_HELP: What Glass writes to the player's journal. Errors always; the level adds the rest. At Verbose and Trace, the targets narrow it. The display and the frames daemon follow the level from their next start.
GLASS.MANAGER_LOG_TARGETS: Targets, all when none is ticked
GLASS.MANAGER_LOG_EMPTY: No lines from Glass in the journal.
GLASS.MANAGER_ST_SHARE_EDITABLE: themes editable from computers on the network
GLASS.MANAGER_ST_SHARE_READONLY: themes readable over the network, not editable
GLASS.MANAGER_PERF_GOVERNOR: Lower the frame rate when the display cannot keep up
GLASS.MANAGER_PERF_GOVERNOR_DOC: When frames keep overrunning with every core painting, the display steps its rate down (60, 45, 30, 20, 15) and says so here; it tries a step back up after a while, and starts over at the set rate with every meter. Off, the set rate is exact.
